UVM Ranked #1 LGBTQ-Friendly College

Luke Dodson, News Reporter
September 28, 2026
Remy Carmichael
Various pride flags are placed outside of the Prism Center, Sept. 25.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:57
Instaread

UVM was ranked as the most LGBTQ-Friendly College by the Princeton Review in “The Best 392 Colleges: 2027 Edition,” published on Aug. 18, 2026.

The ranking criteria is based on student perceptions regarding a culture of equality on campus for all students regardless of gender or sexual orientation. 

“We have 42% students from the incoming class that identify as not cisgender or not heterosexual. There is a community here to build on,” said Dr. Jorge Castillo, associate director of the Prism Center, UVM’s on-campus center for LGBTQ students.

This data on student attitudes came from student body surveys from 392 of the nation’s top colleges according to an Aug. 18 press release.

“UVM has, I think, really committed to making sure that who you are doesn’t define the kind of opportunity that you have,” said Rev. Dr. James Ross II, senior director of intercultural centers and director of the Interfaith Center. 

Trans+ Vermont, a Vermont-wide student club, represents students at Champlain College, Community College of Vermont, Middlebury College, St. Michael’s College and UVM. 

“We obviously are known for having a big LGBT population,” said UVM sophomore Skye Bivens, co-chair for Trans+ Vermont. “I came up here from the South as a trans woman, feeling that I needed to go somewhere that I could feel like I could be open and I could talk.”

UVM senior Ambrose Moore, a member of Trans+ Vermont, talked about the wide visibility of support on campus.

“You go up to teachers’ offices in Old Mill, and they’ll have little pride flags up front, and that visibility does flag as a queer individual. That does flag you are a safe person.” he said.

Moore also has had a positive experience with receiving gender-affirming care from Student Health Services.

“I found that extremely helpful, knowing off the bat that the student health services would have my medications, my prescriptions, especially with the bold attacks on gender affirming care,” said Moore.
